question: Captain Marvel, Earth's Protector costs {3}{W}{W} and entered this turn. Her power-up ability costs {5}{W}{W}. Does her mana cost reduce only the generic {5}, leaving me to pay {2}{W}{W}, or does the {W}{W} in her mana cost also reduce the {W}{W} in the power-up cost?

expected.shortAnswer: The white mana in her mana cost reduces the white mana in the power-up cost and the generic reduces the generic, so the ability costs {2} this turn.
expected.answer: 702.193b Generic mana in the permanent’s mana cost reduces generic mana in the cost to activate its power-up ability. Colored and colorless mana in the permanent’s mana cost reduces mana of the same type, and any excess reduces that much generic mana. (See rule 118.7.)

source.questionAuthorship: The question is this project's own natural-language phrasing of what the cited rule states, asked about a real card with the keyword; the answer is the rule's own text, verbatim. Scryfall carried no WotC ruling for any Marvel Super Heroes card and the rule has no Example: line when this case was authored, so the rule's own text is the official source. This is a second rule-text case for Power-up (the mechanic-pool case is power-up-abomination-activate-once), so it carries no pool.

whyHard: Most cost reductions in Magic reduce only generic mana, so players assume the colored part of a power-up cost must always be paid in full; power-up reduces colored mana by matching colored mana in the permanent's own mana cost.
